verdict.summary: A typical early-stage multi-tenant AI agent is ineligible for Spotify production distribution because Extended Quota requires a registered organization, a launched service, and at least 250,000 MAUs. You may build and test with up to five allowlisted users in Development Mode, but wider distribution requires Extended Quota approval. Avoid voice-enabled Spotify control, training or ingesting Spotify Content into an AI or machine-learning model, and prohibited monetization on a Streaming SDA.
verdict.activeEffort: The guide estimates several hours of registration, configuration, documentation, eligibility, and submission work, plus a 1–3-day Development Mode pilot; this does not overcome the MAU requirement.
verdict.waitTime: Up to 6 weeks (official), if Spotify accepts an Extended Quota application; resubmissions may restart another six-week SLA (community-reported).
verdict.mainGate: Extended Quota eligibility: a company-email application from a legally registered organization with a launched service and at least 250,000 MAUs.

recommendation.text: Use one Spotify Web API application with a server-side Authorization Code OAuth flow for all tenants; each end user authorizes the same client ID. Use Development Mode only for a five-user prototype, and pursue wider rollout only if the organization can satisfy Extended Quota eligibility or receives written permission.

essentials.text: Access tokens last 1 hour. Authorization Code exchanges return refresh tokens; Dashboard-app refresh tokens last 6 months from user authorization, and refreshing does not extend that lifetime. Persist a replacement refresh token when returned; otherwise retain the existing one, and require reauthorization after expiry or revocation.

sources.quote: Access tokens are intentionally configured to have a limited lifespan (1 hour)
Refresh tokens issued to apps registered in the Developer Dashboard have a lifetime of 6 months.
Refreshing an access token does not extend the refresh token's lifetime.
When a refresh token is not returned, continue using the existing token.

essentials.text: Register every callback in Dashboard app settings and send an exactly identical redirect_uri during authorization and token exchange, including case and trailing slash. Use HTTPS except for loopback IP literals; localhost is prohibited.

sources.quote: The value of redirect_uri here must exactly match one of the values you entered when you registered your application, including upper or lowercase, terminating slashes, and such.
Use HTTPS for your redirect URI, unless you are using a loopback address, when HTTP is permitted.
localhost is not allowed as redirect URI.

essentials.text: New apps begin in Development Mode. The owner needs Premium, and only 5 authenticated and allowlisted Spotify users can use the app; Development Mode is explicitly unsuitable as a business foundation.

sources.quote: Newly-created apps begin in development mode .

Up to 5 authenticated Spotify users can use an app that is in development mode
It is intentionally limited and should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business on Spotify.

essentials.text: Rate limits are app-level in a rolling 30-second window; no numeric threshold was published in the researched source. Handle HTTP 429, honor Retry-After in seconds, and back off. Development Mode apps under one developer account share a quota budget.

sources.quote: Spotify's API rate limit is calculated based on the number of calls that your app makes to Spotify in a rolling 30 second window.
The header of the 429 response will normally include a Retry-After header with a value in seconds.
If you have multiple apps in Development Mode, the quota for all of those apps is shared under a single budget.

essentials.text: If eligible, complete Spotify's four-step Extended Quota questionnaire with app information, imagery, APIs/SDKs, terms, policy, and design materials. Spotify reviewers test the app and may follow up by email; official turnaround is up to about 6 weeks.

detail.text: Log into the Spotify Developer Dashboard with a Premium Spotify account, create an app, select “Web API,” enter the user-visible app name and description, and accept the Developer Terms. Treat the description as consent-screen copy and keep the client secret private.

sources.quote: Log into the dashboard using your Spotify account.
Create an app and select "Web API" for the question asking which APIs are you planning to use.
Enter an App Name and App Description of your choice (they will be displayed to the user on the grant screen), put a tick in the Developer Terms
Always store the client secret key securely; never reveal it publicly!

steps.title: Configure server OAuth and callback allowlisting

detail.text: In the app settings, add the production HTTPS callback URI exactly as your backend will send it. Implement Authorization Code on the server using https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize and https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token; encrypt refresh tokens at rest and never expose the client secret to browsers.

detail.text: Confirm that the applicant is a legally registered organization, has a launched active service, and can substantiate at least 250,000 MAUs. If any condition is absent, do not submit as though the app is production-eligible; seek written provider guidance instead.

detail.text: After written approval, verify that the allowlist restriction is removed, monitor app-level rate limiting, retain only necessary user data, and provide a working account-disconnect and deletion path. A Spotify-replacement experience requires Spotify's prior written permission.
